transcript:
"This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour."
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
President Trump is considering a trilateral meeting in China with Chinese leader Xi Jinping
and Russian leader Vladimir Putin.
Trump is scheduled to travel to China next month for the APEC summit, which Putin is
also expected to attend, NPR's Deepa Shivaram reports.
Before departing for Kansas for a rally, Trump fielded questions from reporters about the
war between Russia and Ukraine.
He said he would potentially meet with Xi and Putin together, but not to discuss Ukraine.
The conversation, he said, would have to be about nuclear weapons and denuclearization.
Trump's remarks come as the president has been more critical of Ukraine's President
Volodymyr Zelensky.
In the same gaggle, Trump said Zelensky hasn't been listening to him and suggested that someone
else should negotiate on Ukraine's behalf to end the war.
Deepa Shivaram, NPR News, the White House.
Trump has endorsed Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in his bid for reelection
next week.
As NPR's Daniel Estrin reports, Netanyahu is now promising Israeli voters if he's reelected,
he and Trump will target Iran.
Trump said on social media he may soon need Israel's help to "finish the job" in Iran,
and that only Netanyahu would help.
Trump's endorsement is a major boost for Netanyahu.
Israeli elections are being held next week, and Netanyahu is trailing in the polls against
the opposition front-runner Gadi Eisenkot.
Netanyahu released a campaign video saying if he's reelected, he'll, quote, "destroy
the Iranian threat," and he'll have two years to do it, he says, while Trump is still
in office.
A person briefed on the matter not authorized to speak publicly told NPR, Trump and Netanyahu
have discussed the possibility of a new attack on Iran.
Daniel Estrin, NPR News, Tel Aviv.
The Supreme Court has declined to hear the case of a national labor relations board member
fired by President Trump.
The legal challenge is seen as a test of the reach of presidential power, as NPR's Kristen
Wright reports.
Fired National Labor Relations board member Gwynne Wilcox said President Trump didn't
have the authority to remove her from the job.
The Supreme Court's decision to not hear her appeal leaves in place a lower court ruling
that said Trump's firing was a lawful exercise of executive authority.
Trump's ouster of Wilcox and other officials has tested the independence of federal agencies
to operate freely from presidential control.
The justices overturned that 1935 precedent when the court backed Trump's firing of a
Democratic member of the Federal Trade Commission in June.
Wilcox was the first black woman to serve on the Labor Relations Board, created to protect
the rights of workers in the private sector.
Kristen Wright, NPR News, Washington.
Overnight curfews have been put in place in parts of France after violence and looting
swept through major cities over the weekend.
The country's prime minister, Sebastian Le Corneux, gave local authorities the power to
impose such curfews to counter what he calls delinquents and thugs.
The majority of U.S. stocks outside of AI and tech fell today.
This is NPR News from Washington.
Federal authorities have charged 28 foreign nationals in California, who they say have
illegally registered and voted in U.S. elections.
It's an escalation in the fight between the Trump administration in California that came
into focus last week, when the Justice Department sued the state.
Data show that non-citizens voting is incredibly rare and has not been shown to change the
outcome of races.
Hollywood just had a surprisingly strong weekend, and NPR's Bob Mandela reports the emphasis
is definitely on the surprise.
The number one film this weekend was the martial arts action flick Street Fighter, but it's
the number two film that's causing a stir.
I really feel you did nothing wrong.
I did not.
In You Can See Everything, Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes, who's currently serving
a prison sentence for defrauding investors, is interrogated by absurdist comedian Nathan
Fielder.
Does any part of you worry about me being here 24/7?
I don't think so.
But what if I see something that makes you look bad?
Produced in secret, the almost three-hour movie was on no one's radar until two months
ago.
Then a scene from it went viral, as did talk of a mid-film surprise.
And this weekend, with spoiler-averse crowds flocking to fewer than 1,000 theaters, you
can see everything posted the second best opening ever for a documentary.
Bob Mandela, NPR News.
Japan is launching a spacecraft to bring back samples from Phobos, one of the Martian moons.
Scientists hope the five-year mission will reveal how the moon formed, potentially shedding
light on the origins of life in the solar system.
Japan's leading the international effort, with support from NASA and other space agencies,
the mission aims to return to Earth in 2031.
This is NPR News from Washington.

topics.text: Trump considers a trilateral meeting with Xi Jinping and Putin at the APEC summit in China
Trump endorses Netanyahu ahead of Israeli elections, with Netanyahu promising action against Iran
Supreme Court declines to hear fired NLRB member Gwynne Wilcox's challenge to Trump's removal
Overnight curfews imposed in parts of France after weekend violence and looting in major cities
Federal authorities charge 28 foreign nationals in California with illegally registering and voting
Documentary 'You Can See Everything' with Elizabeth Holmes and Nathan Fielder posts strong opening weekend
Japan launches spacecraft to bring back samples from Mars moon Phobos, targeting 2031 return
